51565421.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to human recombinant Gal-1 assessed as dissociation constant by ITC analysis

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - Isothermal titra: Isothermal titration calorimetry was performed with a Nano ITC Isothermal Calorimeter (TA Instruments). Needle and cell concentrations, injection volumes, and time intervals between injections were varied to obtain sufficient heat production per injection to allow good peak integration, and sufficient time between injections to allow the return to equilibrium. Each titration involved 20 injections of 2.5 μl of ligand solution (5 mM) at 3 min intervals into the sample cell (200 μl) containing human rGal-1 (50 μM) at 298 K. Ligand solutions were prepared by dissolving the ligands in PBS buffer (20 mM phosphate buffer, 150 mM NaCl, pH 7.4) at 298 K. The titration cell was continuously stirred at 300 rpm. The heats of dilution of ligands in the buffer were subtracted from the titration data. Fitting was performed using the NanoAnalyze software to determine the dissociation constant (Kd) and the enthalpy change (ΔH). The stoichiometry (n) was fixed as 1.0.
original_paragraph.Results and Discussion - Isothermal titr: To provide complementary evidence on glycan-binding preferences towards synthetic ligands, ITC determinations were also carried out for the interaction of a set of three preferentially recognized glycans towards Gal-1 (Fig. 4). Due to the relatively low affinity of human galectins for monovalent glycans (>50 μM), the “low c-value” method was used for ITC measurements, with the stoichiometry (n) fixed to 1.00. The measured thermodynamic parameters are presented in Table 2.
original_paragraph.Figure 4 caption: Fig. 4. Interactions of human rGal-1 with the three highest-binding synthetic ligands by ITC. Experimental calorimetric data associated with the isothermal titration at 298 K of rGal-1 with (A) lactose (Lac), (B) 7, (C) 6 and (D) 4 by ITC.
